Recording Ops includes recording agent health, deployment, RDP OCR/metadata and recording storage. Permissions and session I/O policies decide who can open which targets and which I/O rules apply.

My Workspaces (under My Workspace) is the end-user connection area for assigned spaces. Remote access is the operator connection area if you have rights to connection destinations. Just opening the page interface is not proof of session - a real session shows a non-empty session ID and a connecting or connected log area.

Service health, encryption backup and restore, and post-change auditing.

After deployments or configuration changes, ensure you ensure HTTPS health and that your admin session is still working. Check compliance & evidence → audit trail for unexpected errors. Configuration → Server → Service Logs helps check service-side log output in the event of startup or runtime problems.

Configuration → Security → Encryption Settings includes backup and restore for encryption material (export, import and optional super admin plain text export if your role allows it). Encryption key sets cover the server standard and named master encryption keys, including rotating and re-encrypting after key changes. These bottles protect cryptographic custody - they are not a complete application database backup device. Have an external recovery path available for PostgreSQL and host configuration before performing a destructive database initialization.

After a large deployment or a destructive database initialization, verify that endpoint enrollment, password recovery, and the elevation channel are still working before treating the system as ready. Never perform a destructive database initialization without first preparing a recovery path.
Bestaetigen Sie nach the Bereitstellung HTTPS-Gesundheit and Admin-Session.

keys.en_text: The line is split on shell operators (; && || | &). Each segment is evaluated independently and the first denied segment refuses the whole line, so a blocked stage cannot ride on an allowed one.

Before tokenizing, the raw segment is scanned for command substitution $(...) and backticks, parameter expansion ${...}, process substitution <(...), and ANSI-C / hex / unicode escapes ($'...'). Any hit is denied immediately — the engine will not try to
The segment is tokenized into an argument vector using shell-like quoting rules. An unparsable segment (unbalanced quotes, etc.) is treated as obfuscated and denied.

Leading wrappers are peeled off so policy sees the real inner program: sudo (and its -u/-g options), env (and its options + VAR=val assignments), the flagless wrappers nohup, nice, command, exec, time, setsid, stdbuf, ionice, timeout and a leading backslash, and shells (bash, sh, dash, zsh, ash, ksh, csh, tcsh) — a shell with -c has its inner command string re-tokenized (e.g. bash -c
After stripping, the argv is checked for eval of dynamic input and base64-decode pipelines. These are denied because they hide the eventual command from static inspection.

Every token is lowercased and the argv is joined by single spaces to form the canonical command; a whitespace-collapsed form is also produced to defeat keyword-splitting tricks. Matching always runs against these canonical forms, never the raw string.

The always-on baseline dangerous-command blocklist is applied first and can never be re-enabled by an operator allow rule (deny-wins). Then operator deny rules (deny always wins), then — if a fail-closed allowlist is enforced — anything not matched by an allow rule is denied.

keys.en_text: This document is a customizable template. The customer organization decides whether the content is right, who must read it, and how often. A rendered document is not training delivery and is not a control assessment.

Completion records show that a named person read and affirmed a specific document version at a specific time. They are evidence of training records (NIST AT-4) and support the delivery side of awareness training (AT-2, AT-3, CMMC 3.2.1, 3.2.2). Content, audience, and frequency stay with the customer organization. Reading and affirming is NOT a practical exercise and must not be offered as evidence for 800-172 3.2.2e. No percentage here says a control is Met or that any certification exists.

800-172 3.2.2e requires practical exercises on current threats, with feedback to participants and supervisors. This product does not run exercises, phishing simulations, or tabletops, and it reports no evidence for 3.2.2e.

Covered means a document exists in the library and cites a clause of that standard. It does not mean anyone has read the document, and it is not a control assessment. Completion records come from assigned programs and signed attestations, and the compliance verdict belongs to your assessor.
